examples.en: I drew the pattern to embroider on the bag myself.

examples.ko: 이 도안대로 뜨개질하면 쉽게 만들 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you knit following this pattern, you can make it easily.
I downloaded a free pattern from the internet.
The design is complicated, so it's hard to color in.

examples.ko: 케이크 위에 올릴 도안을 골라 보세요.
examples.en: Please pick a design to put on top of the cake.
Place the pattern on the fabric and trace it.

explain: 만들거나 그리기 전에 준비하는 밑그림이나 설계도를 말해서, 뜨개질·자수·색칠 공부·공예에서 많이 써요. 완성된 '디자인' 전체보다는 따라 그리거나 따라 만드는 그림이라는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: I drew a flower pattern to put on the scarf.
phrases.nuance_ko: 만들기 전에 밑그림을 준비한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means preparing an underdrawing before making something.

phrases.en: I found a knitting pattern online.
phrases.nuance_ko: 따라 하면서 만들 수 있게 그려 놓은 설계도예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A guide drawn so you can follow it while making something.

phrases.en: I colored it as the design showed, and it turned out pretty.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-대로'를 붙여 밑그림을 그대로 따른다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-대로' means following the design exactly.

explain_en: It is the base drawing or pattern prepared before making or drawing something, so it is common in knitting, embroidery, coloring books and crafts. It feels less like a finished 'design' and more like a drawing you follow.

t90.ax: Place the pattern on the fabric and trace it.

examples.ko: 거리에서 한 아저씨가 아코디언을 연주하고 있어요.
examples.en: A man is playing the accordion on the street.

examples.ko: 아코디언 소리를 들으니 유럽 여행이 생각나요.
examples.en: Hearing the accordion reminds me of my trip to Europe.
I signed up for an accordion class.

examples.ko: 할아버지가 젊었을 때 아코디언으로 노래를 반주하셨대요.
examples.en: I heard Grandpa used to accompany songs on the accordion when he was young.
This piece is played on accordion and guitar.
It's a house with a door that folds like an accordion.

explain: 외래어 표기는 '아코디언'이에요. 악기를 말할 때는 '아코디언을 연주하다'처럼 '연주하다'와 자주 써요. 주름이 접히는 모양 때문에 '아코디언 문', '아코디언 커튼'처럼 비유로도 써요.

phrases.en: My grandfather plays the accordion.
phrases.nuance_ko: 악기 이름과 가장 자주 쓰는 동사 짝이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common verb pairing for this instrument.

phrases.en: I can hear accordion music from far away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 악기의 소리를 말할 때 쓰는 간단한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simple phrase for the sound of the instrument.

phrases.en: I installed an accordion door in the bathroom.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주름처럼 접히는 문을 비유로 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative name for a folding, pleated door.

explain_en: The standard spelling of this loanword is '아코디언'. For the instrument it commonly goes with '연주하다', as in '아코디언을 연주하다'. Because of its folding pleats, it is also used figuratively in '아코디언 문' and '아코디언 커튼'.

examples.en: The students recite a poem in the classroom.

examples.ko: 저는 그 시를 처음부터 끝까지 암송할 수 있어요.
examples.en: I can recite that poem from beginning to end.

examples.ko: 선생님이 앞에 나와서 암송해 보라고 하셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher told us to come to the front and recite.
The child reciting the multiplication table was cute.

examples.ko: 어제 외운 문장을 친구 앞에서 암송했어요.
examples.en: I recited the sentences I memorized yesterday in front of my friend.
I attend a group where we recite Bible verses.

explain: '외우다'는 머릿속에 기억하는 일이고, '암송하다'는 외운 것을 소리 내어 말하는 일까지 포함해요. 그래서 시, 구구단, 기도문처럼 말해서 들려주는 것에 잘 어울려요. 일상 대화에서는 '외워서 말하다'라고도 많이 해요.

phrases.example: 이 문장을 소리 내어 암송해 보세요.
phrases.en: Try reciting this sentence out loud.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수업에서 선생님이 시킬 때 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase teachers often use in class.

phrases.en: Yesterday I recited a poem in front of my friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체 과거형으로, 외운 것을 말해서 들려준 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Polite past tense, for having said a memorized text aloud.

phrases.en: I memorized the whole multiplication table.
phrases.nuance_ko: '외우다'는 머릿속에 기억하는 일이고, '암송하다'는 그것을 말하는 일까지 포함해요.
phrases.nuance_en: 외우다 is memorizing in the head, while 암송하다 also includes saying it aloud.

explain_en: '외우다' is about fixing something in memory, while '암송하다' includes saying it aloud. So it suits things you say for others to hear, like poems, the multiplication table or prayers. In everyday talk people also say '외워서 말하다'.

t90.ax: The students recite a poem in the classroom.

examples.en: Prize money is given to the prizewinners of the contest.
The list of prizewinners is posted on the website.
Among this year's prizewinners, there is even an elementary school student.
The prizewinners are invited to the award ceremony next week.
Unfortunately, I didn't make it among the prizewinners.
Everyone was nervous on the day the prizewinners were announced.

explain: '입상하다'(상위에 들어 상을 받다)와 짝으로 알아 두세요. '우승자'는 1등을 가리키지만 '입상자'는 등수 안에 들어 상을 받은 사람들을 두루 말해요. 대회, 공모전, 시상식 이야기에서 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I won a prize in the drawing contest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 입상자와 짝이 되는 동사로, 상위 등수에 들어 상을 받는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb paired with 입상자, meaning to place high enough to win a prize.

phrases.en: The prizewinners will be announced next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대회 결과를 알리는 공지에서 자주 봐요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often seen in announcements of contest results.

phrases.en: Prizewinners, please come to the front.
phrases.nuance_ko: 입상자와 비슷하게 상을 받은 사람이지만 시상식에서 더 널리 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 입상자 but more widely used at award ceremonies.

explain_en: Learn it as a pair with '입상하다' (to place and win a prize). '우승자' refers to the first-place winner, while '입상자' covers everyone who placed and received a prize. It is used often when talking about contests, competitions and award ceremonies.

t90.ax: The list of prizewinners is posted on the website.

examples.en: I decided to humbly accept my teacher's advice.
Even if the result is bad, you have to accept it humbly.

examples.ko: 그는 비판을 겸허히 듣고 고개를 끄덕였어요.
examples.en: He listened to the criticism humbly and nodded.

examples.ko: 상을 받고도 겸허히 소감을 말해서 보기 좋았어요.
examples.en: He gave his acceptance speech modestly even after winning, which was nice to see.

examples.ko: 자신의 실수를 겸허히 돌아보는 시간이 필요해요.
examples.en: You need some time to humbly reflect on your own mistakes.

examples.ko: 새 팀장님은 후배들의 의견도 겸허히 들어 줘요.
examples.en: The new team leader humbly listens to the junior staff's opinions too.

explain: '겸손하게'와 뜻이 비슷하지만 더 격식 있고, 말보다는 글이나 뉴스, 발표에서 많이 나와요. 보통 '받아들이다, 인정하다, 듣다' 같은 말과 함께 써요.

phrases.en: He always learns with a humble attitude.
phrases.nuance_ko: '겸허히'의 형용사형으로 명사 앞에 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective form, placed before a noun.

phrases.en: I listened to the criticism humbly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '겸허히'와 뜻이 같고 조금 더 부드럽게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '겸허히' but sounds a bit softer.

phrases.en: Even when praised, she speaks modestly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '겸허히'보다 일상 대화에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used more in everyday conversation than '겸허히'.

explain_en: It is close to '겸손하게' (modestly) but more formal, and it shows up more in writing, news and speeches than in casual talk. It usually goes with verbs like '받아들이다', '인정하다' and '듣다'.

t90.ax: I decided to humbly accept my teacher's advice.

en: to be embarrassed; to be abashed; to be sheepish

examples.en: I called the wrong name, so I felt a bit sheepish.
I felt awkward at being praised, so I just smiled.
He scratched his head as if embarrassed.

examples.ko: 계면쩍기도 하고 고마워서 아무 말도 못 했어요.
examples.en: I felt both awkward and grateful, so I couldn't say anything.
I made a mistake in front of my friend and laughed sheepishly.
Everyone suddenly looked at me, and I feel awkward.

explain: '쑥스럽다'와 비슷하지만 '계면쩍다'는 실수하거나 칭찬받아서 어색하고 멋쩍은 느낌이 커요. '계면쩍게 웃다', '계면쩍은 듯이'처럼 웃거나 머리를 긁적이는 모습과 자주 같이 나와요.

phrases.en: He laughed sheepishly while scratching his head.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실수했거나 칭찬받아서 어색할 때 짓는 웃음을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the awkward smile of someone who made a mistake or got praised.

phrases.en: He said hello with an embarrassed look.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ' 형태로 뒤의 명사를 꾸며서 사람의 모습을 그릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The -ㄴ form modifies a noun to describe a person's look.

phrases.en: Singing in front of friends feels a bit awkward.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 느끼는 어색함을 해요체로 말하는 기본 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic polite present form for how awkward you feel right now.

explain_en: It is similar to '쑥스럽다' but stresses the awkward, sheepish feeling after a mistake or a compliment. It often appears with smiling or scratching one's head, as in '계면쩍게 웃다' and '계면쩍은 듯이'.

t90.ax: He scratched his head as if embarrassed.

en: to be honored; to be glorious

examples.en: I'm truly honored to receive the award.

examples.ko: 오늘 이 자리에 서게 되어 영광스러웠어요.
examples.en: It was an honor to stand here today.
I captured the glorious moment in a photo.

examples.ko: 선생님과 함께 일하는 것은 영광스러운 일이에요.
examples.en: Working with you is an honor.
I was so honored that I cried.

examples.ko: 우리 팀을 대표하게 되면 영광스러울 거예요.
examples.en: It will be an honor if I get to represent our team.

explain: 인사말에서는 '영광이에요', '영광입니다'를 더 자주 써요. 영광스럽다는 형용사라서 '영광스러운 일'처럼 뒤의 말을 꾸밀 수 있어요. 높은 사람이나 큰 행사에서 감사를 말할 때 어울려요.

phrases.example: 이렇게 영광스러운 자리에 초대해 주셔서 감사해요.
phrases.en: Thank you for inviting me to such an honored occasion.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사나 모임을 높여서 말할 때 쓰는, 뒤의 말을 꾸미는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifying form, used to speak respectfully of an event or gathering.

phrases.en: It is an honor to work with you.
phrases.nuance_ko: '영광스럽다'보다 인사말에서 더 자주 쓰는 짧은 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shorter expression used more often than 영광스럽다 in greetings.

phrases.en: I consider it an honor to be invited.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일을 영광으로 여긴다고 말할 때 쓰고, 공손한 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say you regard something as an honor, with a polite tone.

explain_en: In greetings Koreans more often say '영광이에요' or '영광입니다'. '영광스럽다' is an adjective, so it can modify a noun, as in '영광스러운 일'. It fits when thanking someone senior or speaking at a big event.

p.n: 명예롭다 describes an honorable thing, not the speaker's feeling, so it doesn't fit this sentence.

examples.en: This award is a great honor for me.
He won the glory of victory.
The honor went to all of the players.

examples.ko: 이런 영예가 저에게 올 줄 몰랐어요.
examples.en: I never thought such an honor would come to me.

examples.ko: 영예와 책임은 항상 함께 오는 법이에요.
examples.en: Honor and responsibility always come together.

examples.ko: 그녀는 오랜 노력 끝에 영예의 자리에 올랐어요.
examples.en: After long effort, she rose to a place of honor.

explain: '명예'와 비슷하지만 '영예'는 큰 상이나 업적처럼 빛나는 일을 얻었을 때의 자랑스러움에 가까워요. '영예를 안다', '영예를 얻다'처럼 쓰고, 말보다 글이나 시상식 연설에서 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: Our team won the honor of the championship.
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰 상이나 업적을 얻었을 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for winning a big prize or achievement.

phrases.en: I regard this prize as a great honor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시상식 연설에서 고마움을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in award speeches to express gratitude.
phrases.en_equiv: to regard it as an honor

phrases.en: It is an honor to stand here.
phrases.nuance_ko: '영예'와 비슷하고 말할 때도 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Close to 영예 and more common in speech.

explain_en: Close to 명예, but 영예 is the proud, shining feeling of earning something big like a major prize or achievement. It pairs with '영예를 안다' and '영예를 얻다', and shows up more in writing and award speeches than in casual talk.

en: to be elated; to be triumphant

examples.en: The winning players walked out looking triumphant.
My younger sibling is full of pride after getting 100 on the test.
He received the prize with a triumphant look.
He was so full of himself, and he ended up making a mistake.

examples.ko: 칭찬을 한 번 들었다고 너무 의기양양해졌어요.
examples.en: You got way too cocky just because you heard one compliment.

examples.ko: 의기양양할 때일수록 말과 행동을 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: The prouder you feel, the more careful you should be with your words and actions.

explain: 성공하거나 칭찬받아서 자랑스러운 마음이 겉으로 드러날 때 써요. 보통 '의기양양하게', '의기양양한 표정'처럼 모습을 설명할 때 많이 나와요. 반대말은 '의기소침하다'예요.

phrases.example: 그는 상을 받고 의기양양하게 집에 돌아왔어요.
phrases.en: He came home triumphantly after winning the prize.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-게'를 붙여 행동하는 모습을 자랑스럽게 설명할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-게' it describes an action done in a proud, triumphant manner.

phrases.example: 의기양양한 표정으로 친구들에게 점수를 보여 줬어요.
phrases.en: He showed his score to his friends with a triumphant look.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자랑스러운 마음이 얼굴에 드러난 모습을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes pride showing on one's face.

phrases.en: The player who won the match looks elated.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 보이다'로 겉모습이 자신감에 차 있다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-아/어 보이다' it says someone looks full of confidence.

explain_en: It is used when pride from success or praise shows on the outside. It mostly appears in forms like '의기양양하게' or '의기양양한 표정' to describe someone's look. Its opposite is '의기소침하다'.

t90.ax: He received the prize with a triumphant look.

examples.ko: 이번 우승의 가장 큰 공로자는 골키퍼예요.
examples.en: The biggest contributor to this victory is the goalkeeper.

examples.ko: 마을 발전에 힘쓴 공로자들에게 상을 드렸어요.
examples.en: We gave awards to the people who contributed to the village's development.
She is the unsung hero of this project.
I was chosen as a distinguished contributor and received a certificate of commendation.

examples.ko: 공로자를 위한 작은 행사가 내일 열려요.
examples.en: A small event for the contributors will be held tomorrow.
People are curious who the real contributor is.

explain: '일등 공로자', '숨은 공로자'처럼 칭찬할 때 자주 써요. 비슷한 말로 '일등 공신'도 있어요.

phrases.example: 이번 성공의 일등 공로자는 우리 팀장님이에요.
phrases.en: The top contributor to this success is our team leader.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 큰 도움을 준 사람을 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to praise the person who contributed the most.

phrases.en: The cleaning staff are the unsung heroes of the event.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈에 잘 띄지 않지만 큰 역할을 한 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to someone who played a big role without being noticed.

phrases.en: That player is the main reason for the victory.
phrases.nuance_ko: '일등 공로자'와 거의 같은 뜻으로 편하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same as 일등 공로자 and used casually.

explain_en: It is often used in praise, as in '일등 공로자' (top contributor) and '숨은 공로자' (unsung hero). A similar expression is '일등 공신'.

examples.ko: 사람들은 이것을 금세기 최고의 발명품이라고 불러요.
examples.en: People call this the best invention of this century.

examples.ko: 이 작가는 금세기 가장 위대한 소설가로 평가받아요.
examples.en: This author is regarded as the greatest novelist of this century.

examples.ko: 금세기에 들어와 기술이 정말 빨리 발전했어요.
examples.en: Since entering this century, technology has developed really fast.

examples.ko: 금세기 중반에는 인구가 줄어들 것이라고 해요.
examples.en: They say the population will shrink by the middle of this century.
We are people living in this century.

examples.ko: 금세기 들어 날씨가 이상해졌다고 말하는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people say the weather has become strange in this century.

explain: '이번 세기'보다 격식 있는 글말이에요. 쓰는 때에 따라 가리키는 세기가 달라지는데, 요즘은 보통 21세기를 말해요. '금세기 최고의 발명'처럼 평가하는 글에서 많이 봐요. 발음이 비슷한 '금세'(곧)와는 전혀 다른 말이에요.

phrases.example: 이 작품은 금세기 최고의 영화로 불려요.
phrases.en: This work is called the best film of this century.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무엇이 이번 세기에서 가장 뛰어나다고 평가할 때 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Most often used to judge something as the best of this century.

phrases.example: 금세기 들어 기술이 아주 빠르게 발전했어요.
phrases.en: Technology has advanced very quickly since this century began.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이번 세기가 시작된 뒤의 변화를 말할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about changes since the start of this century.

phrases.en: This building was built at the beginning of this century.
phrases.nuance_ko: '초'를 붙여서 이번 세기의 처음 무렵을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 초 points to the early years of this century.

explain_en: It is a more formal, written way to say 'this century'. Which century it points to depends on when it is written, and today it usually means the 21st. You often see it in evaluations like '금세기 최고의 발명'. It is completely different from the similar-sounding '금세' (soon).

examples.ko: 그 가수의 무대 의상은 꽤 도발적이에요.
examples.en: That singer's stage outfit is quite provocative.
He answered the provocative question calmly.
Many people say the ad is too provocative.
His way of speaking sounded provocative, and it upset me.

examples.ko: 이 그림은 색이 강하고 도발적이어서 눈에 띄어요.
examples.en: This painting has strong colors and is provocative, so it stands out.

examples.ko: 그의 태도는 도발적이지 않고 아주 부드러웠어요.
examples.en: His attitude was not provocative at all and was very gentle.

explain: '도발적이다', '도발적인 ~'처럼 써요. 말이나 행동에서는 상대를 자극해서 싸움을 거는 느낌이고, 패션이나 광고에서는 과감하고 시선을 끄는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: The reporter asked a provocative question.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-인' 형태로 명사를 꾸며서, 상대를 자극하는 말에 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form is often used for words that provoke the listener.

phrases.en: This ad is a bit provocative.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체로 어떤 것이 과감하고 자극적이라고 평가할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite form for judging something as bold or provocative.

phrases.example: 그는 일부러 도발적으로 말해서 분위기를 흔들었어요.
phrases.en: He spoke provocatively on purpose and shook up the mood.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사형으로 말하는 태도를 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form describes someone's manner of speaking.

explain_en: It is used as '도발적이다' or '도발적인 ~'. For words and actions it feels like provoking someone into a fight, while for fashion or ads it feels bold and attention-grabbing.

t90.ax: Many people say the ad is too provocative.

examples.en: On the weekend I rode a bike on the Han River bank.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 오면 둔치 주차장이 물에 잠겨요.
examples.en: When it rains a lot, the riverside parking lot gets flooded.
We spread a mat on the riverside and ate fried chicken.
Every evening I run along the riverside.

examples.ko: 강 둔치에는 운동 시설이 잘 되어 있어요.
examples.en: The riverside has good exercise facilities.
Access to the riverside was blocked because of the flood.

explain: '강가'와 비슷하지만, 물가 옆에 평평하게 만들어 놓은 공원이나 운동 공간을 가리킬 때가 많아요. '한강 둔치'처럼 강 이름과 같이 자주 써요.

phrases.en: We ate fried chicken at the Han River bank park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 강 이름과 같이 가장 자주 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common form, used with a river name.

phrases.en: I parked at the riverside lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 강가 옆에 만든 시설을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to facilities built beside a river.

phrases.en: I exercise at the riverside every evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: 평평한 운동 공간으로 쓸 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when it serves as a flat exercise space.

explain_en: It is similar to '강가' (riverside), but it often points to the flat park or exercise area made beside the water. It is often used with a river name, as in '한강 둔치'.
